doc.title: Genevieve Rose interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 14, 1998

chapter: Bass history, future and the scene
title: Upcoming gigs and closing
summary: She mentions Jazz in July and an October gig with Sheila Jordan, then the interview ends.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Okay. Well I think you ought to move to Utica then. We’ll give you enough to pay your gas. Well this has been fascinating talking to you. I wondered if there’s anything that you’d like to take an opportunity to say that I haven’t asked you about.
Oh boy. Off hand I can’t really think about it.
What’s the next kind of important gig you have coming up? Any name people?

That’s hard to say. I mean I know like I’ll be doing the Jazz in July workshop in the summer as a kind of like a faculty member, and I did that last year too, as the house rhythm section for vocalists. And I’ve got something that should be, I think it’s October 17th with Sheila Jordan and Harold Danko as a piano player, and Greg Caputo is the drummer, and that’s at the Iron Horse in Northampton. But that’s a little far off right now. But that will be one of the first gigs under my own name, so that will be nice.
Well you’re certainly rubbing shoulders with some good company.

I enjoy it yeah. It’s great. I think it’s important to be able to perform and have the experience playing with experienced musicians, I learn so much from that, every performance, so I’m really grateful for that.
Well the music’s been good to you and I think you’re being good to the music, so I wish you the best in your career.
Thanks for being here today. It was a pleasure, thank you very much. I enjoyed this, thank you.
